what_this_is: Made-up technique rows for the cross-medium test: 20 invented techniques from four invented sources (board game design, radio drama, museum exhibits, mobile game tutorials), each with crossing fields, the vocabulary their terms come from, and a goal in a fifth medium. No row describes anyone's real research.

request.goal: a sales page for a budgeting app

rows.name: One card stays face down until the last round
rows.description: Each player keeps one card hidden until the final round, when all are turned at once.

needs.says: something worth not knowing yet

produces: players stay until the end to see the reveal

rows.name: One shared score track everyone can see
rows.description: All scores move on one track in the middle of the table.

needs.says: players who care how they stand against others

produces: every move is felt by the whole table

rows.name: A first-turn card that says exactly what to do
rows.description: Each player starts with a card listing the three actions of their first turn.

needs.says: a first action that can be named in a sentence

produces: new players act without reading the rulebook

rows.name: Only four of the best tile
rows.description: The strongest tile has four copies; once taken they are gone.

needs.says: something players already want

produces: players act sooner

rows.name: Each player picks a named role with a short backstory
rows.description: Players choose a role card with a name and two lines of backstory before play.

needs.says: a role close enough to the player's own life

produces: players argue for their role as if it were them

rows.name: The narrator speaks to the listener as their younger self
rows.description: Each episode is a letter the narrator reads aloud to 'you, ten years ago'.

needs.says: a listener who recognises the situation described

produces: the listener hears their own choices in the story

rows.name: Open in the middle of an argument
rows.description: The episode starts mid-argument; how it began is told later.

needs.says: a strong middle moment to start in

produces: listeners stay to learn how it started

rows.name: A sound tells the place before anyone speaks
rows.description: Each scene opens with three seconds of its place: rain, a kettle, traffic.

needs.says: a place with a sound of its own

produces: the listener knows where they are at once

rows.name: The same last line every episode
rows.description: Every episode ends with the narrator's same short sign-off.

needs.says: a line short enough to repeat

produces: listeners say the line along with the narrator

rows.name: The narrator says what they do not know
rows.description: When a fact is uncertain the narrator says so plainly instead of guessing.

needs.says: a listener who keeps listening long enough to hear the doubt

produces: the rest of the story is believed

rows.name: A replica visitors may touch beside the original
rows.description: Next to a glass case stands a copy visitors can pick up.

needs.says: an object small enough to handle

produces: visitors understand the object's weight and size

rows.name: Each room asks one question on its door
rows.description: The door of every room shows one question that the room answers.

needs.says: a question the visitor has not answered yet

produces: visitors walk in looking for the answer

rows.name: A wall of pins, one for every visitor's home town
rows.description: Visitors add a pin for where they come from on a large wall map.

needs.says: enough earlier visitors to fill the wall

produces: new visitors see they are one of many

rows.name: A timeline painted on the floor of the corridor
rows.description: Walking the corridor moves the visitor through the years painted underfoot.

needs.says: a sequence that has a clear order

produces: visitors always know how far along they are

rows.name: The first room is free; the rest need a ticket
rows.description: Anyone can walk into the first room; a ticket desk sits at its far end.

needs.says: a first room good enough to want more

produces: visitors buy a ticket after seeing what is inside

rows.name: The first level needs one finger only
rows.description: Level one teaches a single tap; every other control arrives later.

needs.says: one action that already does something fun

produces: players finish level one in under a minute

rows.name: A bar fills toward the first reward
rows.description: A bar at the top fills with every action and pays out a reward when full.

needs.says: a reward the player wants

produces: players keep going to fill the bar

rows.name: Name the hero before the first level
rows.description: The player types a name for the hero, and every line of dialogue uses it.

needs.says: dialogue that can carry the player's chosen name

produces: the player feels the hero is theirs

rows.name: Any move in the tutorial can be undone
rows.description: An undo button takes back the last move during the tutorial levels.

needs.says: moves that can be reversed cleanly

produces: players try things without fear

rows.name: Show which friends are playing now
rows.description: The home screen shows friends' avatars who are playing at the moment.

needs.says: players who already trust the friends shown

produces: players join the game their friends are in

mechanism.says: Why a technique works, in words about what it does to a person or a system.

terms.says: An unanswered question holds attention until it is answered.
Seeing where one stands against others makes every change felt.
Naming the one first action removes the cost of deciding where to start.
Something limited feels more valuable and is acted on sooner.
The person reads themselves as the subject, so what happens feels like it happens to them.
Showing where and when first lets the person place everything that follows.
Something met before feels easier, safer and is recognised faster.
Saying plainly what is not known makes the rest more believable.
Trying a thing directly makes it understood and less daunting.
Breaking content into small pieces makes it easier to take in.
People trust a choice others have already made.
Seeing how far one has come and how far is left keeps one going.
Giving something useful first makes the offer that follows feel earned.
Knowing a step can be taken back makes a person willing to try it.

property.says: The abstract property of a person or a system that a technique changes or needs.

terms.says: How long a person keeps paying attention.
How much a person wants to find something out.
How much a person feels they are moving forward.
How much suspense or pressure a person feels.
How hard something feels to do.
How much a person feels in charge of what happens.
How much something seems worth.
How much a person feels something is about them.
How well a person knows where they are and what comes next.
How quickly something is known again.
How easily something is recalled later.
How much a person believes what they are told.
How well a person understands something.
How much a person feels part of a group.
How open a person is to being asked to buy or act.
How bound a person feels to keep going.
